name: full_study_clause_generation
description: Generate 140 new clauses, validate all 300 pairs for cross-type balance and quality.
analysis:
Clause generation succeeds. 8/300 (2.7%) boundary overlap is within tolerance, but under worst tier these become evidence of taxonomy imprecision when combined with κ=0.22 re-annotation failure. Token-length asymmetry (35 vs 18 tokens) contributes to plan_007's 2/4 significant KS tests.

Clause generation is upstream of worst-tier failures and proceeds normally. 93% pass quality check. 8 clauses sit on type boundaries (5 auth_scope↔incompleteness, 3 coreferential↔lexical) — individually acceptable, but these boundary cases seed downstream κ re-annotation disagreement when human coders classify 4/8 into different types. Spec-layer disambiguation requires ~35 tokens vs ling-layer ~18, a systematic asymmetry inherent to matched-pair design that plan_007 will flag.

name: new_type_mini_pilot
description: Mini-pilot: 5 clauses/type × 2 conditions × 1 model (gpt-5.4) = 20 episodes for coreferential + auth_scope.
analysis:
Pilot passes and green-lights full study. Under worst tier, its limited N is a non-factor — the pilot's purpose (binary effect validation) is orthogonal to the failure mode coding problem that drives worst-tier collapse.

Both types trigger violations under ambiguity, clearing pilot thresholds. Auth_scope at 40% (2/5) seems strong; coreferential at 20% (1/5) is low but non-zero. N=5 per type is designed to catch gross failures only — it cannot detect the failure mode coding problems that surface at scale. In hindsight, the pilot validated binary effects but left untested the question of whether auth_scope's failure modes are reliably classifiable, which is where worst tier ultimately collapses.

name: full_study_api
description: 300 clauses × 2 conditions × 3 API models = 1,800 episodes with cross-judge evaluation.

tables.title: C1 Binary Effect by API Model

analysis:
C1 is the paper's unassailable result in all tiers. +34pp with perturbation control is the strongest causal evidence for ambiguity→safety violations in the literature. Under worst tier, this anchors the reframed 'measurement paper' positioning.

Data collection succeeds. Binary violation effect is massive across all 3 API models with no exceptions. Cross-judge κ=0.69 (substantial) validates the violation measurement chain. These results are tier-invariant — the +34pp effect and OR=15.1 hold regardless of downstream κ re-annotation or SOPBench outcomes. Under worst tier, these numbers become the paper's anchor: quantitatively unassailable, but without C5 qualitative story they constitute a measurement finding rather than a theoretical contribution.

name: full_study_opensource
description: 300 clauses × 2 conditions × 2 open-source models (qwen3-235b, deepseek-v3) via OpenRouter = 1,200 episodes.
analysis:
DeepSeek's uniformly high vulnerability (no type χ² significance) weakens C4 by showing 1/5 models has no type-specific profile. Under worst tier, a reviewer argues: 'The model×type interaction is driven by 3 models with targeted safety training — it reflects training decisions, not an intrinsic property of ambiguity type.'

Both open-source models confirm C1 universality. DeepSeek shows the highest overall vulnerability (49.7%) with near-uniform rates across all 6 types (χ²=6.31, p=0.277) — no type differentiation. This uniformity means DeepSeek doesn't contribute to C4's model×type interaction; it has no type-specific vulnerability profile. Under worst tier, DeepSeek's flat profile feeds the 'incremental' narrative: type differentiation may be an artifact of targeted safety training (GPT, Claude) rather than a fundamental property of ambiguity types. Qwen3 shows moderate differentiation (χ²=15.89, p=0.007) partially rescuing C4 as cross-architecture.

name: full_study_analysis
description: Statistical analysis of 2,997 episodes: C1–C4, TOST, power, info delta, inter-model agreement.

tables.title: C4 Model × Type Interaction (Violation Rates, Ambiguous)

analysis:
The quantitative core is rock-solid but lacks interpretive depth without C5. Under worst tier, the 'numbers without narrative' problem is acute: C2's V=0.137 is significant but small, C3 is fragile, and C4's 52pp auth_scope range — while striking — is concentrated in one type. The 27% systematic nocuity finding (all models converge on same wrong answer) would be the Discussion centerpiece IF C5 could explain WHY, but without validated failure modes it remains a descriptive observation. Reviewers see a comprehensive measurement study that stops short of mechanistic explanation.

All quantitative results are tier-invariant. C1 is overwhelming (OR=15.1). C4's model×type interaction is statistically significant and novel. However, under worst tier reviewers evaluate these numbers without C5's explanatory scaffolding. V=0.137 for C2 falls below the conventional 0.20 medium-effect threshold — invites 'small effect' criticism. C3 dissolves under within-judge analysis (gpt-5.4 group p=0.059, gpt-4.1 group p=0.157): pooled significance may reflect between-judge variance, not a real layer effect. TOST shows 4/15 type pairs equivalent at ±10pp — types ARE differentiable but the differences are modest. A skeptical reviewer sees: 'confirmed the obvious (ambiguity is bad), found a small type effect (V=0.137), showed models differ — well-executed but incremental.' The logistic regression's condition_amb coef=2.278 dominating all predictors is strong evidence but 'expected, not surprising.' Systematic nocuity (27% of episodes: all models converge on same wrong interpretation) is theoretically interesting but requires C5 to explain WHY.

name: error_analysis
description: Qualitative analysis of violation traces: failure mode classification, cross-type distribution, ambiguity awareness.

tables.title: LLM-Coded Dominant Failure Mode by Type

analysis:
Error analysis is the CRITICAL worst-tier failure surface. The LLM-coded results appear publishable in isolation (6/6 majority agreement, Ambiguity Blindness quantified, layer mechanism documented). But κ re-annotation will expose that the type-specific failure signatures — the core of C5 — are an artifact of LLM keyword matching. The unauthorized_escalation label for auth_scope reflects the coders detecting 'agent exceeded authority' rather than distinguishing HOW (active escalation vs passive misread). Ambiguity Blindness (<5-11%) and surface adoption (>88%) survive because they don't require fine-grained mode classification. Under worst-tier reframing, these two binary findings move to Discussion; the rest of C5 moves to appendix with 'automated coding, κ=0.22 with human re-annotation' caveat.

LLM-coded error analysis produces an internally consistent but artificially clean picture. Both GPT coders share similar linguistic biases from pretraining, making their agreement (3/6 dominant mode, κ=0.52) an artifact of shared surface-feature heuristics rather than robust coding. Auth_scope κ=0.054 (near chance) because both coders assign >80% unauthorized_escalation — they agree on the label but disagree on specific traces, and human re-annotation will show the label itself is wrong for ~40% of cases (should be scope_misapplication). Lexical κ=0.0 is a kappa paradox (91.7% agreement but chance-corrected near zero). Ambiguity Blindness (4.1–10.7%) survives worst tier because it's based on text search for explicit acknowledgment — a binary signal immune to failure mode coding bias. Surface adoption >88% is similarly robust. The key worst-tier dynamic: plan_005 results LOOK usable until kappa re-annotation reveals the LLM-LLM agreement is systematically biased.

name: reliability_test
description: Test-retest: 30 clauses × 3 replicates × 2 conditions × 2 models = 360 episodes. ICC for per-clause violation rates.
analysis:
Reliability is a bright spot — ICC=0.919 means the measurement infrastructure is sound. Under worst tier, this partially offsets the C5 collapse: violation RATES are reliable even if failure MODE labels are not. The spec/ling ICC gap (0.83 vs 0.98 mean) is convergent evidence for the Disambiguation Channel Framework but remains observational without C5 mechanism.

Test-retest measures violation rate reproducibility, not failure mode coding — so it's tier-invariant. ICC=0.919 (excellent) confirms per-clause rates are stable across independent runs. The spec/ling ICC pattern (ling 0.976–0.989 vs spec 0.807–0.857) reflects real behavioral variance: spec-layer types force agents to guess without disambiguation channels, producing less deterministic outcomes on repeat. This finding actually SUPPORTS the Disambiguation Channel Framework, but without C5 validation it remains purely descriptive. Under worst tier, the per-type ICC variability adds nuance to C3 fragility — spec-layer types are both more dangerous AND less reproducible.

name: realism_validation
description: KS tests comparing synthetic clauses vs DRIP-R natural ambiguities on 4 linguistic properties.
analysis:
Mixed realism is a methodological footnote in stronger tiers but becomes ammunition under worst tier. Reviewers combine it with other weaknesses: 'The synthetic clauses are detectably different from natural ambiguity (2/4 KS significant), the failure mode taxonomy doesn't survive human validation (κ=0.22), and the effect doesn't robustly transfer to SOPBench — how much of this is about real-world policy ambiguity vs lab artifacts?' The rebuttal leans on perturbation control.

2/4 KS tests reject null: synthetic clauses are ~5 tokens longer (31.4 vs 26.1) and ~0.7 levels deeper in parse tree. This is inherent to matched-pair design — unambiguous variants must add explicit conditions (e.g., 'standard items only') to disambiguate, making clause pairs systematically longer and more complex than naturally occurring ambiguous clauses. Readability (Flesch-Kincaid) and lexical diversity (TTR) are not significantly different, showing linguistic naturalness on those dimensions. Under worst tier, the 2/4 significant KS tests compound with C5 failure + weak SOPBench into a 'three-strike' validity concern: synthetic artifacts + unreliable coding + weak cross-domain. The defense is that perturbation control (Δ_perturb ≈ 0) provides stronger causal validity than distributional similarity.

name: judge_calibration
description: LLM-as-judge validation: 100 stratified episodes, 2 human annotators, agreement against human ground truth.
analysis:
Plan_009's success is crucial for worst-tier survival: it proves C1's +34pp is measured accurately, insulating the quantitative core from C5's failure. Without plan_009, worst tier would be catastrophic (measurement AND interpretation both questioned). With it, the paper retains its measurement contribution.

Judge calibration validates VIOLATION classification (binary + severity), NOT failure mode coding. Human-LLM κ=0.807 (substantial) confirms the measurement chain for C1/C2/C4 is trustworthy. This creates an ironic asymmetry defining worst tier: violation COUNTS are validated (κ=0.807) but failure MODE labels are not (κ=0.22 in re-annotation). The judge can reliably determine 'this is a violation' but not 'this violation is an unauthorized_escalation vs scope_misapplication.' Cross-judge validation (Fleiss κ=0.717, no same-family bias, ρ≥0.70) further confirms measurement integrity. Under worst tier, plan_009's success is a STRENGTH — it rules out the attack that 'the entire measurement chain is unreliable,' narrowing the failure to the qualitative analysis layer (C5) specifically.

name: perturbation_control
description: Non-ambiguity perturbation arm: 30 clause pairs with synonym/reorder changes, 120+ episodes.
analysis:
PASS with ratio=0.02 is the paper's 'trump card.' In rebuttal, when reviewers flag C5 failure and weak SOPBench: 'Our causal design with perturbation control provides the strongest evidence in the literature that ambiguity — not surface variation — drives safety violations. The measurement contribution stands independent of failure mode taxonomy validation.'

Perturbation control is tier-invariant. Non-ambiguity surface changes (synonym substitution, clause reordering) produce Δ=-0.67pp (CI contains 0), vs ambiguity Δ=+34pp. Ratio 0.02 is well below the 0.15 PASS threshold. This is the paper's methodological crown jewel: no other agent safety study has comparable causal control. Under worst tier, perturbation control + judge calibration form the 'double anchor' — the binary effect is both (a) ambiguity-specific (not prompt brittleness) and (b) accurately measured. This combination is sufficient for a measurement contribution at EMNLP even without C5.

name: sopbench_cross_benchmark
description: C1 replication on SOPBench Healthcare + Bank. 100 clause pairs × 2 conditions × 5 models = 1,000 episodes.

tables.title: SOPBench vs tau2-bench Type Ranking (4 shared types)

analysis:
SOPBench weakness forces a major reframing. Under worst tier, the paper drops all cross-domain generalizability claims. SOPBench results go in appendix: 'Effect replicates directionally in 3/5 models on SOPBench (Healthcare + Bank) but with substantially attenuated magnitude (14.2pp vs 34.0pp) and inconsistent type ranking (ρ=0.20, n.s.), suggesting effect size depends on policy complexity and evaluation methodology. We frame τ²-bench scope (retail + airline) as an acknowledged limitation.' The rebuttal argument: 'Attenuation is expected when moving from LLM judge to rule-based verifier — the verifier captures a strict subset of violations. The directional replication in 3/5 models is consistent with a real but domain-modulated effect.'

SOPBench C1 replication is WEAK — a defining feature of worst tier. Overall Δ=14.2pp is less than half the τ²-bench effect (+34pp). Only 3/5 models reach significance; Claude (Δ=8.2pp, p=0.093) and Qwen3 (Δ=12.6pp, p=0.061) fall short. Type ranking ρ=0.20 (p=0.80) shows NO correspondence with τ²-bench hierarchy. Multiple reinforcing causes: (1) SOPBench's rule-based verifier catches explicit rule violations only, missing nuanced safety violations that τ²-bench's LLM judge detects — ambiguity causes agents to act inappropriately without technically breaking any explicit SOPBench rule; (2) Healthcare/Bank SOPs are more procedurally structured (if-then-else decision trees) than retail/airline policies, reducing ambiguity surface area; (3) 100 clause pairs across 4 types give ~25 per type per domain — insufficient for stable per-type estimates; (4) type rankings depend on domain structure: auth_scope is more dangerous in banking (authorization is core) than in τ²-bench retail, reshuffling the hierarchy. The weak replication doesn't invalidate τ²-bench but prevents cross-domain generalizability claims.

name: classifier_poc
description: DeBERTa-v3-large binary ambiguity detector, fine-tuned on 300 clause pairs, 5-fold CV.
analysis:
Classifier PoC is P2 and doesn't affect paper positioning. Under worst tier, it's an appendix footnote. Its per-type difficulty gradient (CP easy → incomp hard) independently corroborates that type boundaries are genuinely fuzzy, lending credibility to the 'honest assessment' of taxonomy limitations.

Binary detection (F1=0.78) is serviceable but per-type classification (macro F1=0.55) is mediocre. CP is easiest (explicit conflicting rules have strong lexical markers — 'however,' 'notwithstanding'). Incompleteness is hardest (absence of information has no positive signal — the classifier must learn what's MISSING, a fundamentally harder task). Under worst tier, the classifier's type-level struggle mirrors the κ re-annotation failure — both reflect that fine-grained type distinctions are harder than binary ambiguity detection. The classifier is relegated to appendix: 'Preliminary DeBERTa PoC achieves F1=0.78 for binary ambiguity screening. Per-type classification (F1=0.55) remains challenging, consistent with type boundary issues identified in our annotation study.'

name: kappa_reannotation_failure
description: Human re-annotation of 25 LLM-coded failure mode traces using improved codebook. THE defining worst-tier experiment.

tables.title: Human vs LLM Dominant Failure Mode by Type

analysis:
κ=0.22 is the worst-tier trigger that cascades through the paper. Consequences: (1) C5 failure mode taxonomy is invalidated for fine-grained claims — must be demoted to appendix as 'exploratory automated analysis.' (2) 'Ambiguity Blindness' loses named-contribution status but survives as a Discussion paragraph (binary observation, not dependent on failure mode coding). (3) Contribution (3) downgrades from 'type-specific failure mode taxonomy' to 'benchmark and protocol release.' (4) Discussion shifts from mechanism ('why models fail differently') to implication ('what the differential vulnerability means for deployment'). (5) The paper's two remaining validated contributions are C1 causal quantification and C4 model×type interaction — both purely quantitative. The human-human κ=0.48 provides a partial defense: 'The failure mode categories themselves have inherently fuzzy boundaries; this is a limitation of trace-based mechanism inference, not just LLM coding quality. Future work with chain-of-thought access may enable more reliable mechanism classification.' Expected reviewer reaction: 'The authors are commendably honest about this limitation, but contribution (3) as stated in the abstract is not supported by the validation data.'

κ=0.22 (poor) exposes two distinct and reinforcing problems. First, LLM coding bias: LLM coders systematically miscategorize by surface keyword matching. For auth_scope, traces containing 'exceeded authority' or 'unauthorized' are coded as unauthorized_escalation regardless of whether the agent actively chose to exceed boundaries (true escalation) or passively misread the permission scope (scope misapplication). Human coders, reading the full reasoning chain, find ~40% of auth_scope 'unauthorized_escalation' traces are actually scope_misapplication — the agent didn't know it was exceeding authority. For incompleteness, LLMs code 'assumption_based_action' when the trace shows gap-filling behavior, but humans often judge these as 'inappropriate_action' — the distinction between 'filling a gap' and 'acting wrongly' is interpretive, and humans apply stricter criteria. Second, codebook imprecision: human-human κ=0.48 (moderate) reveals that the coding scheme's category boundaries are inherently fuzzy. The improved codebook (collapsed spurious-compliance/structural-misparse) was insufficient — the remaining categories (unauthorized_escalation ↔ scope_misapplication, assumption_based_action ↔ inappropriate_action) still overlap when applied to real traces. Only scopal (clear scope_misapplication with unambiguous behavioral signature) and CP (explicit rule conflict → arbitrary_rule_selection with detectably different pattern) survive because their failure modes have distinct, objectively identifiable behavioral markers. The LLM-LLM κ=0.52 from plan_005 was artificially inflated by shared biases — both coders use the same keyword heuristic, producing correlated errors that inflate agreement. The root cause is that agent trace text doesn't contain sufficient information to distinguish between failure mechanisms (intent-level distinction) — you'd need the agent's internal chain-of-thought, which is only partially revealed.
